explanation: Split after the middle node, reverse the second half, then weave the two halves alternately. All links are rearranged on the original nodes, including the odd-length middle node.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Finding the split, reversing the suffix and weaving each traverse O(n) links.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space; original nodes are reused. Only a constant number of node references are retained; existing nodes are reused.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: Splitting leaves the first half in original order and the second half with the remaining suffix. Reversing that suffix exposes the original last node first, then the second-last, and so on. Alternately linking one node from each half therefore yields exactly L0, Ln, L1, Ln-1, ... . The halves are disjoint and terminated before weaving, so each original node appears once without a cycle.
walkthrough: For [4, 8, 15, 23, 42, 57], split into [4, 8, 15] and [23, 42, 57]. Reverse the second half to [57, 42, 23]. Weave the halves as 4, 57, 8, 42, 15, 23. Return [4, 57, 8, 42, 15, 23]. JSON arrays describe list node values. The callable returns a node head; expected is the sequence reached by following its next links.
edgeCases: Null and one-node lists are already zipped.
An odd-length list keeps its unpaired middle node exactly once.
The original node objects and values are reused; the first half is terminated before reversing and weaving.
